stories.headline: Meridian puts Atlas-3 reasoning model in the API today
stories.standfirst: Atlas-3 ships with a 400,000-token context window and, according to one reporter, undercuts the company's previous frontier tier on price.
body: Meridian released Atlas-3 on Thursday and made it available in its API the same day. The company gives the context window as 400,000 tokens and said it did not plan a staged rollout or a waitlist.

Reporting from The Ledger adds a detail Meridian did not state: the model is priced below the company's previous frontier tier. The researcher Nina Okafor pointed to the evaluation results rather than the context window as the more consequential change.

The claims sit in different registers. Availability and context length come from Meridian. The pricing position is a reporter's characterisation, and the benchmark reading is one researcher's interpretation of results the company published.

stories.headline: Corvid ships Kestrel accelerator to cloud partners
stories.standfirst: The company put the gain at 3.1 times its previous generation, measured on internal benchmarks it has not published.
body: Corvid Systems said its Kestrel accelerator began reaching cloud partners on Monday. The company put the training throughput gain at 3.1 times its previous generation, measured on benchmarks it has not released.
A rival, Thorne Labs, said separately that its MI-series parts begin sampling next quarter. It offered no comparable throughput figure.

stories.headline: Dutch regulator opens inquiry into three training datasets
stories.standfirst: The authority said it is examining whether the datasets contain personal data gathered without a lawful basis.
body: The Dutch data protection authority opened a formal inquiry on Wednesday into three datasets used to train large language models. The regulator said it is examining whether they contain personal data collected without a lawful basis.
Two of the three dataset maintainers confirmed they had been contacted. The third did not respond to a request for comment.

stories.headline: Halden AI raises $600 million at a $14 billion valuation
stories.standfirst: Three people briefed on the terms described the round, which the company has not announced publicly.
body: Halden AI has raised $600 million at a valuation of $14 billion, according to three people briefed on the terms. The company declined to comment.
The round has not been announced. Two of the three people said the terms include a liquidation preference above the prior round.

stories.headline: Researchers report prompt injection reaching production agents
stories.standfirst: A paper describes an attack that survives three published defences, and the authors say two vendors have confirmed the finding.
body: Researchers at Verity Lab published a paper describing a prompt injection technique that survives three published defences. The authors say two vendors have confirmed the finding and are preparing mitigations.
Neither vendor is named in the paper. One later confirmed the contact; the other declined to comment.

stories.headline: Benchmark audit finds nine of fifteen evaluations flawed
stories.standfirst: The audit reports contamination or scoring errors in most of the evaluations it examined, and names the affected suites.
body: An audit published Tuesday reports contamination or scoring errors in nine of the fifteen evaluation suites it examined. The authors name each affected suite and publish their methodology.
Three maintainers acknowledged the findings. One disputed the contamination claim and said the overlap the auditors found was intentional.

stories.headline: Lumen opens its coding agent to all paying customers
stories.standfirst: The company said the agent is out of preview and included at no extra cost on existing plans.
body: Lumen said its coding agent left preview on Thursday and is now included for all paying customers at no additional cost.
The company did not give usage limits. Two customers said the preview had capped runs per day.

stories.headline: Northgate says its assistant now handles claims end to end
stories.standfirst: The insurer said the system closes routine claims without a human reviewer, a claim its regulator has not assessed.
body: Northgate said its assistant now processes routine claims from filing to payment without a human reviewer. The company said the system handles about a third of its claim volume.
The figure is the company's own and has not been reviewed by its regulator, which said it does not comment on individual firms.

stories.headline: Aster publishes weights for its 8-billion parameter model
stories.standfirst: The release is under a licence permitting commercial use, with a restriction on training competing models.
body: The release is under a licence permitting commercial use, with a restriction on training competing models. The company said it would publish further detail later this week.

body: The company gave no volume figures and declined to name customers. The company said it would publish further detail later this week.
